result.text: A university enrollment system involves the following steps: Prospective students submit an application online.
The admissions office reviews the application and supporting documents.
If documents are missing, the applicant is notified to provide the missing items.
Upon receiving all documents, the application is evaluated by the admissions committee.
Concurrently, the finance department processes any application fees or waivers.
If the application is accepted, an acceptance letter is sent.
Otherwise, a rejection letter is sent and the process ends.
After being accepted, the student must then confirm enrollment by a specified deadline; otherwise the application will be canceled.
If the student confirms, they receive orientation materials and the IT department sets up student accounts for email, online portals, and library access.
If the student is international, the international student office assists with visa processing.
The student obtains a student ID card and starts creating their study plan, which includes: Meeting with an academic advisor.
Selecting courses.
Resolving any schedule conflicts.
The student begins attending classes.
Throughout each semester, the student may add or drop courses within the add/drop period.
At the end of the semester, grades are posted, and the student can review them online.
If the student has any grievances, they can file an appeal, which includes: Submitting an appeal form.
Meeting with the appeals committee.
Awaiting a decision.
The process repeats each semester until the student graduates or withdraws.

result.process_description:
A university enrollment system involves the following steps:
Prospective students submit an application online.
The admissions office reviews the application and supporting documents.
If documents are missing, the applicant is notified to provide the missing items.
Upon receiving all documents, the application is evaluated by the admissions committee.
Concurrently, the finance department processes any application fees or waivers.
If the application is accepted, an acceptance letter is sent.
Otherwise, a rejection letter is sent and the process ends.
After being accepted, the student must then confirm enrollment by a specified deadline; otherwise the application will be canceled.
If the student confirms, they receive orientation materials and the IT department sets up student accounts for email, online portals, and library access.
If the student is international, the international student office assists with visa processing.
The student obtains a student ID card and starts creating their study plan, which includes:
Meeting with an academic advisor.
Selecting courses.
Resolving any schedule conflicts.
The student begins attending classes.
Throughout each semester, the student may add or drop courses within the add/drop period.
At the end of the semester, grades are posted, and the student can review them online.
If the student has any grievances, they can file an appeal, which includes:
Submitting an appeal form.
Meeting with the appeals committee.
Awaiting a decision.
The process repeats each semester until the student graduates or withdraws.

result.rule: When the description says a repeated cycle of activities continues until the process participant reaches one of several named exit outcomes, and each outcome is an action or state that is stated as a distinct branch: Model a merge gateway that rejoins the flows before the repeated cycle's first activity, and place an exclusive decision gateway after the cycle's last decision point. Give that gateway one outgoing flow back to the merge for continuing the cycle, and one outgoing flow for each named exit outcome. Model each exit outcome as a task that the process performs, and connect each task to the end of the process. Do not replace an outcome that the description states as an action with only an end event or an intermediate event.

When the description says a repeated cycle ends when the actor reaches one of several named outcomes, such as completing or leaving, and each outcome is stated as a distinct result: Model each named outcome that ends the repetition as its own activity on a separate exit branch of the loop's decision gateway, labeled with the outcome's wording from the description, so that every stated outcome has a corresponding activity and no outcome is folded into a generic continuation or an unlabeled end.

When the description says a repeated sequence of steps ends only when an actor reaches one named outcome or performs another named action, so that each named exit outcome is a distinct stated result: Model a decision gateway that leaves the repeated sequence. Place each named exit outcome as its own task or branch on that decision, in the order the description gives, and connect the remaining branch back to the start of the repeated sequence. Do not merge the exit outcomes into one task, and do not leave a named outcome without its own branch or task.

When the description says the process ends with one of several alternative outcomes, each stated as an action performed on the item the process handles, and the outcome is chosen at a decision point: Model each outcome as a task that performs the stated action, placed on its own branch after the decision gateway, and give each such task its own end event. Do not connect the decision gateway directly to bare end events named after the resulting state.
